item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 30, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian Naira opened today, Friday, October 30, 2026, holding firm against the United States Dollar across both the official foreign exchange window and the parallel market, following sustained liquidity interventions by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and healthy diaspora inflows. At the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the spot exchange rate traded at N1,346.86 per dollar during early morning transactions. Commercial banks and corporate importers observed orderly liquidity conditions as FX demand for trade obligations, tuition fees, and capital repatriation continued to be met across authorized channels. In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, street traders and Bureau De Change operators across major economic centers, including Lagos, Abuja, and Kano, quoted buying rates around N1,375 per dollar, while selling rates hovered around N1,385 per dollar. The price gap between the official market and the parallel window remains narrow. Financial analysts attribute the relative stability of the local currency to Nigeria’s solid foreign reserve buffer, which remains well above $55 billion, enabling the central bank to cushion short-term demand shocks and maintain stability across trading channels. Market experts expect trading to remain steady throughout the business day as routine demand is steadily absorbed by market liquidity. item.title: PSC promotes 2 DIGs, 10 AIGs, 17 CPs, 3,800 others
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Police Service Commission (PSC) has approved the promotion of more than 3,800 senior police officers, including two Deputy Inspectors-General of Police (DIGs), 10 Assistant Inspectors-General of Police (AIGs) and 17 Commissioners of Police (CPs). The promotions followed the officers’ successful participation in promotion examinations and oral interviews conducted by the commission. A statement issued by the PSC on Thursday said the approvals were granted at its plenary meeting in Abuja, presided over by its Chairman, DIG Hashimu Salihu Argungu (rtd). The two officers elevated to the rank of DIG are AIG Olaolu Adegbite, Head of INTERPOL National Central Bureau, Abuja, and AIG Dankombo F. Morris, who heads Zone 4 Headquarters, Makurdi. Adegbite holds a BA in Russian Language from the University of Lagos and an MA in Philology from the Pushkin Institute, Moscow. He is a recipient of the national honour of Member of the Order of the Federal Republic (MFR), a member of the FBI National Academy Associates and an alumnus of Harvard Kennedy School. He previously served as Director of Operations at the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). Morris, who hails from Gombe State, holds a BA in History from the University of Maiduguri and a Diploma in Police Science. He has served as Commissioner of Police in Adamawa State. The 10 officers promoted from CP to AIG are Omosanyin Olusegun, CP Administration, FCID Annex, Ikoyi, Lagos; Ogbodo Ugobueze, CP Anti-Fraud, FCID Annex, Enugu; Ohagwu Felix Ndukwe, CP Ondo State; Taylor Lennox Olanrewaju, AIG/ES, Nigeria Police Cooperative; Regina Cosmas Udoette, CP GI, FCID Annex, Enugu; Afolabi Wilfred Olutokunbo, CP Abia State Command; Nwogoh Martin, CP Airwing; Shetima Jauro Mohammed, CP Nasarawa; Ibrahim D. item.title: NESG: Nigeria’s high production costs threaten industrial competitiveness
item.description: By Favour Ulebor The Nigeria Economic Summit Group has warned that high production costs, unreliable electricity and poor logistics infrastructure are undermining Nigeria’s industrial competitiveness, calling for a council within the Presidency to coordinate industrialisation policies. Co-facilitator of the NESG, Lumun Feese, said Nigeria needed a coordinated approach to industrial development to address structural challenges and enable local manufacturers to compete effectively in African markets. She spoke at a breakout session on building an integrated industrial ecosystem during the 32nd Nigeria Economic Summit in Abuja. Feese said Nigeria had dropped from eighth to 14th position on the African Development Bank’s Africa Industrialisation Index, although she noted that the methodology had changed and more countries had been included in the latest ranking. She said, “We are not maximising our potential and our large economy. “How do we go and compete in South Africa when our cost of production is so high? Feese said the proposed industrialisation, competitiveness and regional integration council would provide a central coordinating platform within the Presidency to align government policies, improve implementation of the National Industrial Policy and strengthen private-sector participation. She said Nigerian businesses needed reliable power, efficient transportation systems and lower production costs to take advantage of the African Continental Free Trade Area, which offers access to a wider continental market. Feese said the recommendations followed consultations on mining, the blue economy, power, oil and gas, and industrial competitiveness. She urged businesses and other stakeholders to sustain their engagement with the NESG’s Industrial Policy Commission, saying coordinated policies and consistent implementation were necessary to achieve measurable industrial growth. Other stakeholders at the session identified limited access to finance, skills shortages, regulatory bottlenecks, security concerns and inadequate export infrastructure as major obstacles to industrial growth. Special Assistant on Strategy to the Minister of State for Industry, Gerald Okunsebor, called for greater awareness of the National Industrial Policy and a clear implementation framework with defined responsibilities, timelines and accountability mechanisms. He said a central knowledge-management system was also needed to ensure continuity in industrial development policies across successive administrations. item.title: Nigeria’s export earnings rise 23.7% to $35.6bn in H1’26
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe Nigeria’s total export earnings rose by 23.7 per cent year-on-year, YoY to $35.64 billion in the first half of 2026 (H1’26), from $28.82 billion in the corresponding period of 2025, driven largely by a surge in petroleum products exports. Analysis of data from the quarterly statistical bulletin, of the Central Bank of Nigeria’s (CBN) for Q2’26, showed that the country’s export earnings increased by $6.82 billion during the six-month period, with petroleum products accounting for about 65 per cent of the growth. Petroleum products exports jumped by 238.7 per cent YoY to $6.31 billion in H1’26 from $1.86 billion in H1’25, representing an increase of approximately $4.45 billion. Crude oil remained Nigeria’s largest individual export category, generating $17.51 billion, up 7.7 per cent YoY from $16.25 billion in the corresponding period of 2025. Gas exports also increased, rising by 4.2 per cent YoY to $6.22 billion from $5.97 billion. Consequently, total exports of crude oil, gas and petroleum products rose by 21.9 per cent YoY to $30.03 billion from $24.63 billion in H1’25. The performance indicates that petroleum-related exports remained the dominant source of Nigeria’s export earnings, accounting for about 84.3 per cent of total exports during the period. Meanwhile, non-oil exports increased by 18.2 per cent YoY to $5.60 billion from $4.74 billion in H1’25. Despite the increase, non-oil exports accounted for about 15.7 per cent of total export earnings, down from approximately 16.5 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025. item.title: From ‘Miracle Girl’ to Purpose: How Esther Longe turned survival into life of impact
item.description: *SHE survived the 2006 crash that claimed 96 lives, battled survivor’s guilt, and spent a decade building a career in marketing before embracing a divine call to ministry. Today, she is redefining leadership through faith, strategy and legacy. By Nkiruka Nnorom The first thing that hits you about Dr Esther Longe is how ordinary she looks. No burn scars. No limp. No visible reminder of a tragedy that wiped out 96 lives in minutes. Only a small scratch. A literal scratch, she calls it. On October 29, 2006, 21-year-old Esther was aboard ADC Airlines Flight 053 from Abuja to Sokoto. The Boeing 737-2B7 crashed shortly after take-off after encountering wind shear, broke up, and burst into flames in a cornfield near Tungar Madaki village, Abuja. 20 YEARS AFTER THE ADC AIR CRASH There were 105 souls on board — 100 passengers and five crew members. Ninety-six died, including the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammadu Maccido; his son, Senator Badamasi Maccido; and Deputy Governor Alhaji Garba Muhammed. Nine survived. Of all the survivors, Esther Kemmer Amoda, now Longe, was the only one without physical injuries. The burden of a miracle Newspapers the next morning called her the Miracle Girl. Television vans camped outside her home. Everybody said the same thing: “God has saved your life for a reason.” At 21, she did not want a reason. She wanted to disappear. “From the onset, I understood that my survival came with a responsibility. But it came with panic attacks and survivor’s guilt,” she tells Weekender. “As a 21-year-old, that was daunting. I did not know what that purpose was. I did not think I had done anything to deserve being saved or singled out.” The years she ran For the next ten years, she ran. She ran into lecture halls and boardrooms. She bagged a BSc in Mass Communication from the University of Lagos, a master’s in Marketing from the University of South Wales, UK, a master’s in Research, and a PhD in Marketing, both from the University of Bath, UK. She became a trained marketing strategist, working with some of the biggest global brands — PwC, GTBank, Pizza Express, and Wrigley’s. She served as a Super Mentor for FCMB SheVentures and a facilitator for the Africa Green Grant Award. She was on track to become a Chief Marketing Officer at a Fortune 500 company. She wanted to be known for what she built, not what she survived. “If I am being honest, I ran and hid,” she confesses. “If you look at me, you would not know I had been through such an experience. It was easy to hide. I did not want to be known for something I had nothing to do with. I wanted to be known for what I had accomplished.” But purpose does not need permission. People who lost loved ones on that flight began to find her. Not to blame her, but to connect. item.title: Omitted candidates: INEC upholds 41 of governorship petitions, rejects 28
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has upheld 41 of the 69 petitions filed against the final list of governorship candidates for the 2027 general election, while rejecting 28. Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee (IVEC) of the commission, Mohammed Kudu Haruna, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday night. According to him, the petitions came from 12 political parties across 26 states. He said, “The complaints concerned the omission of certain political parties, the wrongful inclusion of candidates of political parties whose names were not contained in the membership registers submitted by their political parties, and instances of alleged multiple nominations.” Haruna said the commission examined the complaints against its records and the law. “Following a review of the complaints, relevant records and applicable legal provisions, the Commission found merit in some representations and approved the inclusion of affected candidates and their political parties, while complaints found to be without merit were declined. “In addition, some names that were wrongfully published in the final list were removed after verifying that their names were not on the register. “The Commission also approved the removal of candidates whose nominations were found to be inconsistent with the applicable legal requirements,” the statement said. Although INEC did not name any candidate or state, a source had earlier revealed that the commission’s meeting on Thursday to review complaints from parties and candidates left out of the lists had cleared a former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Prof. Isa Ali Ibrahim Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections, subject to the outcome of pending court cases. The source also said the petition by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, seeking a review of his exclusion from the list, did not succeed. “Yes, Pantami has been cleared,” the source said when asked about the PDP governorship candidate in Gombe State. “He did not succeed,” the source said when asked about Adebutu. On the State Houses of Assembly, the commission said the decisions affecting candidates sponsored by political parties “were informed by specific complaints received and determined in accordance with the law and the Commission’s established criteria.” For those elections, INEC received 61 petitions from 11 political parties across 11 states. Twenty-five succeeded, while 36 failed. The commission said the affected candidates, political parties and states “will be reflected in the updated list on the Commission’s website.” “Once again, the Commission assures the public of its commitment to transparency and the credibility of the electoral process,” the statement said. item.title: 2027: INEC grants provisional clearance to Pantami, Gwarzo – Source
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi & Ben Ngwakwe There were strong indications on Thursday night that the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC might have provisionally cleared a former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Gombe State, Prof. Isa Ali Ibrahim Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections. The clearance of both men is subject to the outcome of pending court cases, it was learned on Thursday night. In Gombe, Pantami’s supporters took over some major areas celebrating the development on Thursday night. INEC officials did not immediately react to Vanguard’s questions regarding the development. But a source said the decisions were reached at the commission’s meeting on Thursday to consider complaints from political parties and candidates whose names were left out of the lists published ahead of the 2027 elections. The source added that the commission had no objection to their candidacies, but that the pending legal proceedings could still affect the final outcome. The development comes after INEC dropped Pantami’s name from the final list of governorship candidates for Gombe State, although he appeared on the provisional list published on August 29. Pantami emerged as the PDP candidate after leaving the All Progressives Congress (APC) on May 19. One of the aspirants for the ticket, Ahmed Mailantarki Mailantarki, challenged his victory in court. A Federal High Court sitting in Gombe nullified the election and ordered a fresh primary, which Pantami won again. His biggest hurdle was the September 24 Supreme Court judgement, which restored Sections 77(5), (6), (7) and 84(2) of the Electoral Act 2026. The provisions bar parties from fielding candidates whose names were not in the membership register submitted to INEC within the stipulated time. Mohammed Haruna, an INEC National Commissioner, had previously said that, in line with the Supreme Court ruling, some parties would not field candidates in 2027. The commission, however, rejected a petition by the PDP governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, who had asked it to review his exclusion from the list of candidates. item.title: Taraba massacre: Reps seek urgent help as death toll hits 60
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina Abuja—The House of Representatives has called for urgent security and humanitarian intervention, following a deadly bandit attack on Binnari community in Karim Lamido Local Government Area of Taraba State, with the death toll reportedly reaching 60. Read Also: Armed bandits raid Taraba community, loot food stores The lawmakers also urged stronger security cooperation among Taraba, Plateau and Bauchi states to tackle the persistent attacks and prevent further loss of lives. The appeal followed a motion on the attack, which reportedly occurred on October 23, 2026, leaving dozens dead and residents displaced. The House called for immediate relief for affected residents and urged the relevant authorities to expedite the completion of the Wase–Karim Lamido road to improve access and security in the area. Contributing to the debate, Minority Leader, Fredrick Agbedi, criticised what he described as the overreliance on resolutions and minutes of silence in response to recurring security crises, insisting on practical measures to protect lives. He called for a technology-driven security response, stressing the need for improved intelligence gathering, surveillance and coordinated operations to confront the attackers. In his response, the Deputy Speaker cited government efforts to address insecurity, including the neutralisation of terrorists, surrenders by insurgents, a reduction in the number of local government areas under insurgent control and increased spending on security. The House’s intervention underscores growing concerns over the humanitarian consequences of repeated attacks in parts of the country and the need for coordinated action by federal and state authorities. The lawmakers urged the relevant agencies to act urgently to restore security, provide relief to victims and prevent further attacks on vulnerable communities. item.title: Ebola: A virus that refuses to disappear
item.description: By Chioma Obinna WHEN late Dr Ameyo Stella Adadevoh insisted that Patrick Sawyer be isolated at a Lagos hospital in July 2014, she was confronting a disease Nigeria had never experienced on that scale. Her decision to trust her clinical judgement, despite the pressure surrounding the patient, became a defining moment in the country’s fight against Ebola. Adadevoh recognised the danger, alerted the authorities and helped trigger the response that eventually contained the outbreak. She contracted the virus and died on August 19, 2014. Nigeria recorded 20 Ebola cases and eight deaths during the outbreak. The country was declared free of Ebola transmission by the World Health Organisation on October 20, 2014. More than a decade later, Ebola continues to challenge public health systems. The reported confirmation on October 20, 2026, of an imported case of Bundibugyo virus disease in a woman who travelled from Uganda and was admitted to a private hospital in Abuja has brought the disease back into focus. A threat that remains Why does Ebola remain such a formidable threat despite advances in medicine, surveillance and outbreak response? The answer lies in the virus’s biology, limited treatment options for some species, exposure to infected wildlife, international travel and weaknesses in health systems. Fear, misinformation and distrust can further undermine efforts to control outbreaks. Adadevoh’s story remains relevant because Ebola’s first encounter with a health system may not appear extraordinary. It may begin with a patient whose symptoms resemble those of a familiar illness and a doctor who must decide whether to look beyond the obvious. The danger behind familiar symptoms For Dr Rotimi Adesanya, a family physician and public health expert, Ebola is dangerous because it can rapidly overwhelm the body. “Ebola Virus Disease is one of the most dangerous infectious diseases known to mankind because of its ability to overwhelm the body’s immune system and cause severe damage to multiple vital organs within a relatively short period,” he said. Early symptoms include fever, headache, weakness, muscle and joint pain, sore throat and fatigue. More severe symptoms, including vomiting, diarrhoea and abdominal pain, may follow. These symptoms can resemble malaria, typhoid and other common infections, making a patient’s travel history and possible exposure important parts of clinical assessment. Symptoms generally appear between two and 21 days after exposure. According to the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), Ebola spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of infected people or deceased patients, infected animals, or contaminated materials. Early identification, laboratory confirmation, isolation, contact tracing and strict infection prevention and control measures are essential to containing outbreaks. item.title: It’s not how much we borrow, but what we build — Tinubu
item.description: *Adds Lagos-Calabar, Sokoto-Badagry highways, power, ports’re drivers of $1trn economy *NLC demands justification for $20.5bn, €1.45bn loans By Johnbosco Agbakwuru and Olayinka Ajayi ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has defended his administration’s external borrowing plans, saying Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, Trans-Sahara Superhighway, electricity grid upgrades and modernisation of key commercial ports in Lagos among others would strengthen Nigeria’s productive capacity. Read Also: Tinubu lands in Saudi Arabia for Umrah According to him, the loans will finance critical infrastructure and investments capable of expanding economic opportunities for future generations. The President’s position came as the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, faulted his request to the National Assembly for approval to obtain fresh external loans of $20.5 billion and €1.45 billion, questioning the justification for continued borrowing despite claims of increased government revenue. In a statement titled “From Reforms to Delivery: Our Infrastructure Investment and Growth Strategy,” Tinubu said the focus should be on the economic value generated by borrowed funds rather than the amount borrowed. “The real question is not how much we borrow, but what we build, what value we create and what future we leave behind,” he said. The President identified the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, Trans-Sahara Superhighway, electricity grid upgrades and modernisation of key commercial ports in Lagos as major projects expected to strengthen Nigeria’s productive capacity. He said investments in healthcare, education and vocational training will complement the infrastructure projects by connecting economic regions, reducing logistics costs, unlocking agricultural and industrial potential and attracting private investment. According to him, the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is expected to reduce logistics costs along its corridor by 15 to 20 per cent and potentially add up to two per cent to Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product, GDP, through increased trade, tourism and industrial activity. The project is also projected to generate about 100,000 direct jobs in construction and engineering, alongside more than 150,000 indirect jobs in logistics, materials and related services. Tinubu said: “We are not simply building highways, we are opening economic corridors, connecting markets, unlocking industries and reshaping Nigeria’s economic geography.” He argued that achieving his administration’s ambition of building a $1 trillion economy by 2030 will require sustained investment in infrastructure to support productivity, industrialisation and trade. “We cannot build a $1 trillion economy with infrastructure designed for an economy a fraction of that size,” he said. item.title: 2027: Pantami, Gwarzo in, Adebutu out
item.description: After more than two weeks of suspense, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) yesterday took a final decision on the fate of candidates nominated by political parties for governorship and House of Assembly seats who were not initially cleared by the commission. The commission’s top officials, after series of meetings with its chairman, Prof Joash Amupitan, cleared former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Isa Ali Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections. The electoral commission, however, rejected a petition by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, seeking a review of his exclusion from the list of candidates. INEC explained that the right of those cleared to contest is subject to the outcomes of pending court cases against them. The commission, however, gave a window of 14 days to those omitted to forward their petitions to the commission for possible review. Our correspondents report that after the close of submission on the 24th, in which all the affected filed their petitions, INEC promised to come up with a final decision on the petitions on the 29th. And after a meeting which lasted for over six hours on Thursday, it declared that some of the candidates have been cleared. A competent source at INEC, who spoke to Daily Trust after the commission’s meeting on Thursday, said the commission received 69 petitions from political parties concerning omitted candidates for governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections. item.title: Makinde warns gaming operators against illegal practices
item.description: By Adeola Badru Oyo State Governor, ‘Seyi Makinde, has warned gaming operators against illegal practices and regulatory non-compliance, saying such activities threaten government revenue, undermine fair competition and erode public confidence in the industry. Makinde said operators must comply strictly with the state’s gaming laws as technological advancements and the expansion of digital platforms continue to create new opportunities and regulatory challenges in the sector. The governor spoke on Thursday while delivering the keynote address at the seventh Annual Stakeholders’ Interactive Forum organised by the Oyo State Gaming and Lottery Board at the Jogor Centre, Ibadan. Represented by the Secretary to the State Government, Professor Musibau Babatunde, Makinde reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to creating a fair, transparent and accountable regulatory environment that would encourage legitimate investments while protecting players and the general public. “Our position as a government is clear. Economic growth must be encouraged, businesses must be allowed to thrive within the law, and the interests of the public must remain protected. “These objectives are essential to building an industry that is productive, responsible, and sustainable,” he said. The governor noted that technological developments, particularly online gaming platforms and mobile applications, had transformed the industry, creating opportunities for investment, employment, innovation and revenue generation. However, he said the developments had also introduced fresh regulatory and consumer protection challenges that required effective supervision and stronger safeguards. According to him, the industry’s contribution to economic development depends largely on the ability of regulators and operators to balance commercial expansion with accountability and public interest. Makinde described the Oyo State Gaming and Lottery Board as critical to maintaining stability in the sector, stressing the need for effective supervision, enforcement of licensing requirements and decisive action against illegal operators. He, however, cautioned that regulation should not become an obstacle to legitimate businesses, insisting that fairness, transparency and consistency must guide the government’s engagement with industry operators. He urged the board to strengthen its institutional capacity, improve engagement with stakeholders and deploy modern technological tools to enhance monitoring, enforcement and regulatory compliance. Makinde also charged operators to make compliance an integral part of their business operations rather than treat it as a mere statutory requirement. He specifically urged them to maintain valid licences, fulfil their tax and levy obligations, keep accurate business records and comply with all applicable regulatory requirements. item.title: Cocoa firm exceeds commercial paper target
item.description: Sunbeth Global Concept Limited has attracted subscriptions exceeding N220 billion for its N150 billion commercial paper offer, reflecting strong investor confidence in the company’s business and growth strategy. The offer exceeded its target by more than N70 billion, representing oversubscription of more than 46.7 per cent. Proceeds will support cocoa procurement for the new season and finance the company’s trading and working capital requirements. The successful offer comes as Sunbeth expands its cocoa sourcing and trading operations alongside its investment in processing. Its planned 70,000 metric tonne cocoa processing plant in Nigeria forms part of a broader strategy to deepen local value addition and supply cocoa products to local, regional and international customers. Commenting on the outcome, Chief Financial Officer, Adeyemi Aduwo, said: “The strong response reflects investors’ confidence in Sunbeth and our growth strategy. We thank our investors and transaction partners for their support. This funding strengthens our cocoa procurement capacity as we continue building an integrated business spanning sourcing, trading and processing.” Sunbeth acknowledged Chapel Hill Denham, its lead arranger, and the participating dealers, advisers and professional partners for their contribution to the issuance. It could add up to two per cent to Nigeria’s GDP through expanded trade, tourism, and industrial activity. ‎ ‎The project is also projected to generate about 100,000 direct jobs in construction and engineering, alongside more than 150,000 indirect jobs in logistics, materials and related services. ‎ ‎According to him: “We are not simply building highways. We are opening economic corridors, connecting markets, unlocking industries and reshaping Nigeria’s economic geography.” ‎ ‎He said the administration’s ambition to build a $1 trillion economy by 2030 would require sustained infrastructure investment to support higher productivity, industrialisation and trade. ‎ ‎“We cannot build a USD 1 trillion economy with infrastructure designed for an economy a fraction of that size,” Tinubu said. ‎ ‎He wrote that improving economic indicators and growing international investor confidence are creating opportunities for Nigeria to attract long-term investment and expand critical infrastructure. ‎ ‎The President said the economic reforms his administration introduced in May 2023 helped restore macroeconomic stability, strengthen public finances, and improve the country’s standing in international financial markets. ‎ ‎He said a $1 trillion economy would not emerge by declaration alone but must be built through sustained investment, higher productivity, industrialisation, and trade, stressing that infrastructure development would be critical to achieving the target by 2030. ‎ ‎In an article titled “From reforms to delivery: Our infrastructure investment and growth strategy,” Tinubu said real Gross Domestic Product growth reached 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, while headline inflation fell to 14.63 per cent in September from 20.98 per cent a year earlier. ‎ ‎He also said gross external reserves rose to $55.1 billion as of October 9, 2026, including about $46 b

item.title: Osimhen welcomes second child with Cameroonian-German girlfriend
item.description: Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen and his girlfriend, Stefanie Ladewig, have welcomed their second child, a baby girl named Liora Audrey. Galatasaray, the Turkish club where Osimhen plays, announced the arrival of the couple’s daughter in a social media post on Thursday. “Our Football A Team player Victor Osimhen and Stefanie have welcomed a baby girl into the world. “We congratulate the couple Victor and Stefanie; we wish their newborn baby Liora Audrey a long, healthy, and happy life!” the post read. The couple’s first daughter, Hailey, was born in October 2022. Ladewig, a Cameroonian-German fashion model and social media influencer, reportedly began dating Osimhen in 2019 when the Nigerian forward was playing for German Bundesliga side Wolfsburg. Earlier this month, reports emerged that Ladewig had been involved in a road accident while heavily pregnant. Turkish media reported that she escaped unhurt in the crash, which involved three vehicles. Meanwhile, Osimhen is expected to feature for Galatasaray in their league fixture against T. Konyaspor on Friday, having been included in the squad for the match. The 27-year-old forward was in impressive form on Monday, scoring twice to help Galatasaray defeat their fierce Istanbul rivals, Fenerbahce, in the city derby. Galatasaray currently lead the league standings after nine matches, while Osimhen has scored eight goals, placing him among the competition’s joint-top scorers. item.title: Everton beat Newcastle 3-1 to reach League Cup quarter-finals
item.description: Everton swept into the League Cup quarter-finals with a 3-1 win against Newcastle on Thursday as they booked a clash against giant-killers Fleetwood. David Moyes’s side took the lead through James Garner’s first-half goal at the Hill Dickinson Stadium. Hayden Hackney doubled the lead with his first goal since his close-season move from Middlesbrough. Everton striker Thierno Barry netted in the second half and Dan Burn’s reply for Newcastle came far too late to stop the Toffees ending their three-match winless run. Chasing their first League Cup final appearance in 43 years, Everton will travel to fourth-tier minnows Fleetwood in the week commencing December 14. The ‘Cod Army’ caused one of the biggest shocks in League Cup history on Tuesday when they beat Premier League champions Arsenal in a penalty shoot-out after a 1-1 draw at Highbury. Everton have never won the League Cup, losing their two final appearances in 1977 and 1984. Everton fans do not need reminding that it is 31 years since the club won the FA Cup in their most recent trophy triumph. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, a noted Everton fan, is old enough to remember that success and he was cheering from the stands as Moyes’s men made light work of their last-16 tie. Newcastle will have the chance for revenge when the sides meet again in the Premier League at St James’ Park on Monday. Everton dropped a pre-match bombshell, saying Jack Grealish was unavailable for selection “due to a breach of club discipline”. Grealish, beset by criticism of his behaviour off the pitch, was reported to have taken an unauthorised absence from training. But the on-loan Manchester City winger’s absence was no problem for his team-mates. – Everton hit their stride – Newcastle tested Jordan Pickford early on when Joe Willock’s low drive was palmed away by the Everton goalkeeper, who repelled Fabian Schar’s long-range strike moments later. Garner steadied Everton’s nerves with a clinical opener in the 34th minute. Hackney teed up Garner just inside the area and the midfielder stretched to guide a fine finish into the far corner for his first goal since January. Everton had hit their stride and Hackney struck on the stroke of half-time. At the climax of a blistering Everton counter-attack, Barry hooked a cross into the six-yard box and Hackney timed his run perfectly to volley past Lukas Hornicek. Frustrated Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle sent on Joelinton, Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa at the interval. Wissa had an immediate chance after sprinting onto Willock’s pass, but he misjudged the high bounce and ended up heading straight at Pickford. It was a costly miss as Barry put the result beyond doubt in the 69th minute. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall provided the cross and Barry lashed home from close range for his seventh goal this season. item.title: 2027: Utomi, Ohaa, Yesufu urge Nigerians to mobilise support for Obi
item.description: Chieftains of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) have urged Nigerians to mobilise grassroots support for the party’s presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, come 2027. The party chieftains, including a political economist, Prof Pat Utomi, Enugu State NDC governorship candidate, Chief Chinyeaka Ohaa and human rights activist, Aisha Yesufu, made the call on Thursday during the Obi-Kwankwaso Town Hall Meeting held in Enugu. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Obi, his running mate, Sen. Rabiu Kwankwaso, and other NDC stakeholders attended the meeting, which attracted a large crowd of supporters. Addressing the crowd, Utomi expressed confidence that the Obi-Kwankwaso presidential ticket would provide the leadership needed to address Nigeria’s economic, political and security challenges. He lamented that Nigeria’s potential to become one of the greatest countries in the world had been undermined by corruption, criminality and disunity. According to him, the time has come for Nigerians to unite and work towards achieving meaningful political change. “We have done our research, and I know that a combination of Peter Gregory Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso will deliver Nigeria,” he said. Utomi urged Nigerians to turn out massively during the elections, vote for their preferred candidates and defend their votes through lawful means. In his remarks, Ohaa, the NDC governorship candidate in Enugu State, described the Obi-Kwankwaso political alliance as a historic opportunity to strengthen national unity and promote inclusive governance. He said the partnership represented the possibility of building political bridges across Nigeria’s geopolitical zones. According to him, the alliance is reminiscent of the historic political understanding between the late Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe and Sir Ahmadu Bello during Nigeria’s early political development. “My message today is simple: we must seize this opportunity and work with our brothers and sisters across the South-South, South-West, North-East, North-West and North-Central to secure an NDC president in 2027,” he said. Ohaa explained that the campaign was not merely about producing a president of Igbo extraction but about establishing a government committed to justice, accountability, security and prosperity for all Nigerians. He expressed confidence that NDC candidates in Enugu State were prepared to earn the trust of voters and secure victory in the elections. Yesufu, a human rights activist, urged Nigerians to take ownership of the 2027 elections by mobilising voters and actively participating in the democratic process. She said the election was not merely about Obi’s presidential ambition but about the collective responsibility of Nigerians to rescue the country from its numerous challenges. item.description: Former Imo State governor, Rochas Okorocha, has faulted the four-year presidency proposed by the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, describing it as a gamble. item.title: [VIDEO] Umrah: Tinubu Arrives In Saudi Arabia
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has arrived in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The President landed at the King Abdulaziz International Airport, Jeddah, on Thursday night. ﻿ He was received by the Nigerian ambassador to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Yakubu Gambo, and Saudi’s head of Royal Protocol, Ahmad bin Thafir. Tinubu is in the country to perform Umrah, an Islamic spiritual exercise involving a pilgrimage to the Holy City. He departed Abuja for Makkah on Thursday afternoon. The event is an opportunity for spiritual reflection, devotion, and prayers for the nation’s peace, unity, stability, and continued progress, Tinubu’s media aide, Bayo Onanuga, said in a statement on Wednesday. According to the statement, the President will perform the religious rites associated with Umrah, seeking Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people. He is expected back in the country next week. The post [VIDEO] Umrah: Tinubu Arrives In Saudi Arabia appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: ‘X-Men,’ ‘Star Trek’ Star Patrick Stewart Dies At 86
item.description: Patrick Stewart, the British Shakespearean actor who became a Hollywood megastar through roles in the “Star Trek” and “X-Men” franchises, has died at the age of 86, an official statement said Thursday. “We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” the statement said. The actor, who hailed from the northern English region of Yorkshire, trod the boards in Britain with the Royal Shakespeare Company before crossing the Atlantic to enjoy an acclaimed career on the US stage and screen. His best known Hollywood roles were as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in “Star Trek: The Next Generation” and Professor Charles Xavier in multiple “X-Men” and related Marvel films. British actor Sir Patrick Stewart arrives to Paramount+ Star Trek Day held at Skirball Cultural Center in Los Angeles, California, on September 8, 2022. Photo by MICHAEL TRAN / AFP “His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre,” the statement said. “He explored the human condition in all its poetic complexity and brought hope not only to the far reaches of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but into science fiction’s most iconic final frontier aboard the Starship Enterprise.” AFP The post ‘X-Men,’ ‘Star Trek’ Star Patrick Stewart Dies At 86 appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: 2027: Tinubu Can Be Sure Of Victory In Imo With My Name On Ballot — Okorocha
item.description: Former Imo State Governor Rochas Okorocha has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu will win Imo State in the 2027 presidential election if he is on the ballot as the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Imo West Senatorial District. Okorocha is locked in a legal battle with his successor, Governor Hope Uzodimma, over the APC ticket for Imo West, with both laying claim to victory in the party’s primary election. ﻿ The APC, however, submitted Uzodimma’s name to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) as its candidate, prompting Okorocha to challenge the decision in court. On Thursday, the Federal Capital Territory High Court ruled that Okorocha secured the majority of votes cast in the primary and should be declared the winner. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today hours after the judgment, Okorocha said his presence on the ballot would guarantee Tinubu’s victory in the state. “What is important to me now is how Asiwaju will be elected in Imo State. With this, my name coming on the ballot paper now, Asiwaju can be sure that his victory is given in Imo State,” he said. The former governor celebrated the ruling, insisting that the judiciary was not for sale. He also said Uzodimma had “met his Waterloo,” alleging that the court had pronounced that his documents “were forged”. Okorocha urged people in the South-East to approach the 2027 presidential election strategically, advising the Igbo to put political calculations ahead of emotions. According to him, supporting Tinubu would amount to a strategic alliance that could benefit the South-East politically in the future. “As Southeasterners, we are not going to politics now with emotions; we have to go to politics with strategy. So, supporting Tinubu for Ndigbo is a strategic alliance,” he said. “We cannot afford to gamble for four years. Any time Nigerians think it is the time for Ndigbo to be president, we should be proper presidents.” Okorocha added that he would work more effectively with other South-East governors to secure Tinubu’s victory in the region if he were placed in charge of the president’s campaign in Imo State. item.title: Paris Gun Attack Leaves One Dead, Five Wounded As Suspect Faces Terrorism Probe
item.description: A man suspected of a gun attack in the Paris suburbs last week that killed one person and wounded five including a child has admitted to “targeting individuals who appeared to be Muslim, African, or North African,” prosecutors said on Thursday. Earlier this week the 39-year-old man, identified as Kevin T., had said he did not “dispute the material facts”, but contested “the racist nature of his crimes”. On Thursday, national terrorism prosecutor Olivier Christen told a news conference that Kevin T. now claims he chose the location for his actions because it was “a hotbed for Islamists”. The victims were shot from a vehicle driving through the towns of Trappes and La Verriere west of Paris. The suspect was detained later Friday with a machine gun and tear-gas grenades in his car. He has since been held in police custody and was set to appear before a judge later on Thursday, Christen said, noting that he had requested that he be held in pretrial detention. France’s counter-terrorism public prosecutor Olivier Christen speaks during a press conference at the Paris Judicial Court, in Paris on October 29, 2026, following the terrorist attack that took place on October 23 in Trappes and La Verriere.Photo by ANNE-CHRISTINE POUJOULAT / AFP Of the four people seriously injured in the attack, “three of the victims remain hospitalised as I speak, and one of them is still in life-threatening condition,” Christen said. He noted the “very high level of preparation” behind the attack. Kevin T. nevertheless denied any “terrorist intent,” viewing his actions as “legitimate,” the prosecutor said. The opening of a judicial investigation by the office of the national anti-terrorism prosecutor (PNAT) allows a judge to take charge of the case, specifically regarding charges of “murder and attempted murder in connection with a terrorist enterprise”. A search of the suspect’s home had uncovered “weapons or weapon components, specifically a magazine, two pairs of brass knuckles, a steel bayonet, and a silencer,” Christen said. Also found were several “books, including a Quran, a Bible, and Adolf Hitler’s Mein Kampf”, as well as stickers celebrating the far-right National Rally (RN) party. Christen said the stickers bore slogans such as “Long live France, RN, proud to be French”, but they were not produced by the party led by Marine Le Pen, who is leading opinion polls to succeed Emmanuel Macron as French president in elections next spring. Kevin T. had told investigators that “he designed the stickers found in his home himself, and then ordered them to be manufactured via Amazon more than a year ago.” The suspect had said that “he is neither a member of nor a sympathiser with any political party”, Christen said.
